definition: pjm-h11 card C-1: the 2020 key added to PJM_SEAM_LADDER_BY_YEAR, a rule-23 re-derivation of the already-armed measured seam ladder on one more year (zero ScenarioConfig fields, zero scalars, zero free parameters). Keeper recipe 2026-09-11-pjm-d4-4-gasoutage replayed at HEAD 3b71948 with that single code delta. Every year solved in its OWN shard container, one year per container, both cross-year warm-start knobs off (rule 36 [R-YEAR-ISOLATION]); composed in the parent at zero LP. Arm-vs-control over 2021-2025 is EXACT (max |delta class TWh| 0.000000), so C-1 moves 2020 alone. Class-volume totals vs the outgoing keeper: sum |error| 48.2 -> 47.05; CC_REGULAR +7.50 -> +0.35; COAL_BIT +16.90 -> +22.27. That COAL_BIT move is NOT C-1 -- a same-HEAD control with no C-1 reads +25.16, so the rebuilt pjm_offer_midcurve_condbinned.json carries +8.26 TWh of it and C-1 recovers 2.89. Promoted on the owner's 2026-09-20 ruling with that regression on the record.
market_story: PJM sells into its neighbours off a measured, price-elastic seam ladder rather than a gas-indexed estimate. Each seam (MISO, NYISO, Carolinas, TVA, LGEE) offers eight bands of import and export capability at reference prices derived from the neighbour's own measured hub prices, so the interchange node competes with PJM's internal stack instead of behaving as a fixed schedule -- exports clear when PJM is cheap relative to the neighbour and shut when it is not. Until this run the ladder simply had no 2020 row, so PJM's 2020 seam ran the forecast gas-elastic track while every other year ran the measured one. C-1 closes that hole. Its first-order consequence is that PJM's 2020 exports fall: on 2020's measured neighbour prices the seam clears less PJM energy than the gas-elastic estimate assumed, which withdraws 10.6 TWh of fossil dispatch -- CC_REGULAR first, then coal and peakers, in merit order -- and leaves nuclear, wind, hydro and biomass untouched. That is the ladder behaving as a supply curve should. It is also, measured against EIA-930's 41.6 TWh of 2020 net export, a worse fit than the estimate it replaces, and the export-side shortfall it deepens is now the named open defect: card C-2 established the gap is ~100% export-side, so PJM's remaining seam error is about how much PJM is willing to sell, not about phantom imports.
